extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for computing patent term adjustment (PTA) and reduction under 35 U.S.C. 154 and implementing regulations (37 CFR 1.702–1.704), including when Office actions and applicant conduct generate or reduce PTA. Covers definitions, start/end dates, overlapping periods, and special situations (RCEs, appeals, secrecy orders, remands).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office actions as notifications under 35 U.S.C. 132
rubrics_metrics.description: A written restriction requirement, a written election of species requirement, a requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105, an action under Ex parte Quayle, and a notice of allowability (PTOL-37) are each an action issued as a result of the examination conducted pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 131 and are notifications under 35 U.S.C. 132.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court precedent (e.g., Pfizer v. Lee; Idorsia Pharm. v. Iancu; In re Hengehold; Digital Equipment Corp. v. Diamond) supports treating written restriction requirements and similar examiner requirements/objections as notices under 35 U.S.C. 132. MPEP § 710.02(b) treats written restriction requirements containing no action on the merits as notices under 35 U.S.C. 132 and sets a shortened statutory period for reply of two months under 35 U.S.C. 133.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a)(2) — longer-than-four-months after reply under 37 CFR 1.111
rubrics_metrics.description: The period for adjustment is the number of days, if any, beginning on the day after the date that is four months after the date a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 was filed and ending on the mailing date of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure from four months after filing the reply under 1.111; count days until examiner action or notice of allowance. This implements 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(A)(ii) for replies under 35 U.S.C. 111.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a)(3) — longer-than-four-months after a reply in compliance with 37 CFR 1.113(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period is the number of days, if any, beginning on the day after the date that is four months after the date a reply in compliance with 37 CFR 1.113(c) was filed and ending on the mailing date of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 is a reply to a final Office action; a reply in compliance with 1.113 cancels all rejected claims and removes all outstanding objections/requirements or otherwise places the application in condition for allowance. Any after-final amendment that does not accomplish that is not a reply in compliance with 1.113(c) and will not trigger this four-month measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a)(4) — longer-than-four-months after an appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37
rubrics_metrics.description: The period is the number of days, if any, beginning on the day after the date that is four months after the date an appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37 was filed and ending on the mailing date of an examiner’s answer under 37 CFR 41.39, an action under 35 U.S.C. 132, or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37' requires (1) payment of the appeal brief fee (37 CFR 1.17(b)) (though for briefs filed on or after March 19, 2013 the fee was set to zero) and (2) compliance with 41.37(c) requirements. The statutory phrase 'the date on which an appeal was taken' is interpreted as the date the appeal brief was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a)(5) — longer-than-four-months after a final decision by the Board or a federal court
rubrics_metrics.description: The period is the number of days, if any, beginning on the day after the date that is four months after the date of a final decision by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board or by a federal court in an appeal under 35 U.S.C. 141 or a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 (where at least one allowable claim remains) and ending on the mailing date of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key definitions: 'allowable claims remain in the application' means at least one pending claim not withdrawn and not subject to rejection/objection; examples (A–C) illustrate allowable vs. objected claims. For a Board decision to count, it must sustain or reverse rejections on appeal (or in limited cases a remand may be deemed a decision). A 'final decision' means last decision in the review by the Board (or federal court) that does not require further applicant action to avoid termination; a decision containing a new ground of rejection under 37 CFR 41.50(b) is not 'final' for this purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(a)(6) — longer-than-four-months to issue patent after payment of the issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The period is the number of days, if any, beginning on the day after the date that is four months after the date the issue fee was paid and all outstanding requirements were satisfied and ending on the date the patent was issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relevant 'date issue fee paid and all outstanding requirements satisfied' is the later of the date the issue fee was paid or the date outstanding requirements were satisfied. Filing a priority document (and processing fee) is not an 'outstanding requirement' for this rule because the patent can issue without the priority claim. If prosecution reopens after allowance, the application is not again in condition for allowance until a new notice of allowance/PTOL-85(b) is issued and returned with any remaining requirements met; measure from that later allowed date (see MPEP §1308 and §2732).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(b) — three-year pendency adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: The adjustment period is the number of days, if any, in the period beginning on the day after the date that is three years after the actual filing date of the application and ending on the date a patent was issued, subject to exclusions and limitations in 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(1)(B)(i) and (ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude periods equal to time consumed by: (1) continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b); (2) interference or derivation proceedings; (3) imposition of a secrecy order; and (4) appellate review under specified statutes. Delays requested by applicant (circumstances constituting failure to engage reasonable efforts) are treated under 37 CFR 1.704. Federal Circuit precedent (Novartis AG v. Lee; Mayo Foundation v. Iancu; Ariad Pharm. v. Matal) informs how 'time consumed by continued examination' and related issues are measured and when Office acknowledgments matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'time consumed by continued examination' under 37 CFR 1.703(b)(1) (effective Jan 9, 2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time consumed by continued examination under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) is the number of days, if any, in the period beginning on the date on which any request for continued examination (RCE) was filed and ending on the date of mailing of the notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies regardless of whether an Office action is issued during the period. Multiple RCEs can produce multiple (possibly non-contiguous) excluded periods measured from each RCE filing date to the subsequent notice of allowance. An RCE filed after a notice of allowance gives rise to a second excluded period beginning on its filing date. A period that results from the Office sua sponte reopening prosecution (without an RCE by applicant) generally is not 'time consumed by continued examination' unless an RCE is later filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(c) — periods for interference or derivation
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment under 37 CFR 1.702(c) is the sum of: (1) the number of days, if any, from the date an interference or derivation proceeding was instituted to involve the application and ending on the date that proceeding was terminated with respect to the application; and (2) the number of days, if any, from the date prosecution in the application was suspended by the Office due to interference/derivation proceedings not involving the application and ending on termination of the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only non-overlapping days are summed. If an interference is declared following an RCE, the period after termination of the interference through mailing of the notice of allowance can be excluded as time consumed by continued examination at the applicant's request (see Mayo Found. and related precedent).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(d) — periods for applications under a secrecy order
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment under 37 CFR 1.702(d) is the sum of non-overlapping periods including: (1) days the application was maintained sealed under 35 U.S.C. 181; (2) days from mailing of an examiner’s answer under 37 CFR 41.39 in the application under secrecy order to the date secrecy order was removed; (3) days from notification that an interference/derivation would be instituted but for the secrecy order to removal of secrecy; and (4) days from notification under 37 CFR 5.3(c) to mailing of the notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 and 37 CFR 1.311.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sum non-overlapping periods only. These subperiods capture different ways secrecy orders can delay issuance; measure each from the specified start and end events.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(e) — periods for successful appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment under 37 CFR 1.702(e) is the sum of the number of days, if any, from the date jurisdiction passes to the PTAB under 37 CFR 41.35(a) (or 41.31 for earlier regimes) and ending on the date of a final decision in favor of the applicant by the Board or a federal court in an appeal under 35 U.S.C. 141 or a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal Circuit precedent (SawStop; Chudik) requires both (1) reversal of an adverse determination of patentability and (2) issuance of the patent 'as a result of that reversal' for the adjustment to apply. A claim that issues only after substantive post-appeal prosecution/amendment that materially changes the claim may not satisfy 'issued under a decision in the review reversing an adverse determination of patentability.'

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(f) — determination of overall adjustment and overlapping periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The adjustment runs from the patent expiration date as set in 35 U.S.C. 154(a)(2). Periods of delay attributable to grounds in 37 CFR 1.702 that overlap shall not cause the aggregate adjustment to exceed the actual number of days the issuance of the patent was delayed (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal Circuit (Wyeth v. Kappos) held that periods overlap under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(A) only if the measuring periods occur on the same calendar day. The term shall be adjusted for the sum of non-overlapping periods calculated under 1.703(a)–(e), less reductions under 1.704. Certificate-of-mailing/transmission dates under 37 CFR 1.8 are not used for PTA calculations (actual date of receipt/OPSG deposit dates are used). Applicants should use USPTO EFS/OPSG, Priority Mail Express ® to Addressee, or permitted facsimile to secure earliest filing/receipt dates and should verify OPSG entries and request corrections prior to grant. PTA calculations at grant will use OPSG dates; subsequent adjustments require a fee and statement per 37 CFR 1.704 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.703(g) — disclaimer limits to adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: No patent whose term has been disclaimed beyond a specified date shall be adjusted under 37 CFR 1.702 and 1.703 beyond the expiration date specified in the disclaimer (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent includes a terminal disclaimer that limits expiration to an earlier date, PTA cannot extend the patent term beyond the disclaimed expiration date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(a) — reduction of adjustment for applicant failure to engage in reasonable efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment under §§ 1.703(a) through (e) shall be reduced by a period equal to the period of time during which the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution (processing or examination) of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant conduct that unreasonably delays prosecution will reduce PTA. The rule provides both a general reduction concept and specific examples/elaborations in subsequent paragraphs and subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(b) — three-month reply rule for applicant delay
rubrics_metrics.description: For grounds of adjustment in §§ 1.702(a)–(e), an applicant is deemed to have failed to engage in reasonable efforts for the cumulative total of any periods of time in excess of three months that are taken to reply to any notice or action by the Office, measuring the three-month period from the date the notice/action was mailed or given to the applicant. The period of adjustment is reduced by days beginning on the day after the three-month date and ending on the date the reply was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office-set shortened statutory period for reply in the Office action has no effect on this three-month measurement — the three-month threshold is independent. Compute cumulative totals of time in excess of three months for replies to rejections, objections, arguments, or other requests and reduce PTA by that excess time (non-overlapping with other reductions).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(1) — suspension of action at applicant's request
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of action under § 1.103 at the applicant’s request constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts and results in reduction of the PTA by the number of days, if any, beginning on the date a request for suspension under § 1.103 was filed and ending on the date of termination of the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any period of voluntary suspension initiated by applicant under 1.103 is excluded from PTA by subtraction of the suspension interval (non-overlapping with other reductions).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(2) — deferral of issuance under § 1.314
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for deferral of issuance of a patent under § 1.314 constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts and reduces the PTA by the number of days, if any, beginning on the date the deferral request was filed and ending on the earlier of the date a request to terminate the deferral was filed or the date the patent was issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral of issuance requested by applicant subtracts the deferral interval from PTA calculations; measure from the deferral request filing to termination or issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.704(c)(3) — abandonment or late payment (applicant delay) (section begins)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment of the application or late payment (listed as circumstances constituting failure to engage in reasonable efforts) will result in reduction of the period of adjustment to the extent the periods are not overlapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP lists abandonment/late payment as one of the candidate circumstances leading to PTA reduction; subsequent text (not in this chunk) provides the precise measurement rules and effects. Include as an applicant-delay ground to be measured and subtracted per 1.704.
